title: Special Permutations
statement:
`nums` holds `n` distinct positive integers. Call an ordering (permutation) of `nums` special when every two neighbouring values in it divide one another in at least one direction: for each pair of adjacent values `x` and `y`, `x % y == 0` or `y % x == 0`.

Return how many special permutations of `nums` exist, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
constraints: all values in nums are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

Trying all `n!` orderings is hopeless for `n = 14` (about 8.7 · 10¹⁰). But whether the next value may be appended depends only on which values are already used and which one was placed last, not on the order of the earlier ones. So count partial orderings by the state (set of used indices as a bitmask, last index): at most `2^14 · 14` states, each extended in `n` ways.

## Approach

1. Let `dp[mask][last]` be the number of valid orderings of the indices in `mask` that end with index `last`.
2. Seed one ordering for each single value: `dp[1 << i][i] = 1`.
3. Visit masks in increasing order (adding a bit always makes the mask larger). For each state with `ways > 0`, try every unused `next` whose value divides or is divided by `nums[last]`, and add `ways` to `dp[nextMask][next]` modulo `MOD`.
4. The answer is the sum of `dp[full][last]` over all `last`, where `full` has every bit set.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2,3,6]`. The singletons start with 1 way each. Index 2 (value 6) is compatible with both others, while 2 and 3 are not. Masks `{2,6}` and `{3,6}` get 1 way each for both end values. From `[2,6]` (last 6) you may add 3, and from `[3,6]` (last 6) you may add 2; orderings ending in 2 or 3 cannot continue. So `dp[full][0] = 1` (`[3,6,2]`) and `dp[full][1] = 1` (`[2,6,3]`), and the total is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(2ⁿ · n²): each of the `2ⁿ · n` states tries `n` next indices.
- Space: O(2ⁿ · n) for the table.

## Pitfalls

- The divisibility test must go both ways: `a % b` or `b % a`.
- Reduce modulo `10^9 + 7` on every addition; `14!` already exceeds it.
- Every value can start an ordering; seeding only index 0 misses most of them.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dp[mask][last]` | orderings of the indices in `mask` that end at `last` |
| `mask` | bitmask of indices already placed |
| `full` | the mask with all `n` bits set |
| `last`, `next` | the index placed last, and the index tried after it |
| `ways` | count for the current state |
| `total` | the answer so far |
